options.name: repo

notes: If name is omitted, a random human-readable name is generated automatically
Gitignored files matching .worktreeinclude in the primary checkout are copied into the new workspace
.worktreeinclude and --copy-file use gitignore syntax. A file is copied only when it matches and is gitignored, so tracked files are never duplicated
Files that already exist in the new workspace are left unchanged
Symlinks are skipped and are not followed. A .worktreeinclude symlink is not read

.rabi.toml is read from the invoking checkout, or from the selected primary checkout when -R/--repo is supplied. [hooks] setup commands run in the new workspace, in order, and stop at the first failure

setup hooks run only after the repository is trusted. On a terminal, rabi shows the project path and the hook commands and asks 'Trust this project and run its hooks? [y/N]'. No, a non-terminal, stdin or stderr not being a terminal, nonempty CI, --no-input or RABI_NO_INPUT being enabled, or --json fails before creating the workspace. An empty value counts as unset. Run rabi trust add or pass --no-setup. RABI_TRUST_ALL=1 trusts every repository for that process and writes nothing

Hooks and exec receive RABI=1, RABI_WORKSPACE (the workspace name), RABI_WORKSPACE_ID (the ws_ ID, or empty if unrecorded), RABI_WORKSPACE_PATH (the absolute workspace path), and RABI_REPO_PATH (the primary checkout path)

New workspaces are created under $XDG_DATA_HOME/rabi/workspaces/<checkout>-<hash> (default ~/.local/share/rabi/workspaces/...). <checkout> is the canonical primary checkout directory name, so a symlink uses the same directory. <hash> is the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the canonical Git common directory. A relative XDG_DATA_HOME is ignored. workspace-root overrides this and is joined to the repository root
Purpose and links are stored in rabi/workspaces/<id>.json under the Git common directory
Config and state live only under rabi paths. Project markers use .rabi-common-dir; clone staging uses .rabi-clone-

All JSON uses schema 2: {schema:2, command, ok, data, warnings:[{code,message}], error:null|{code,message,details?}}. data preserves partial results and has no top-level version/schema. Parsers must ignore unknown fields. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 operational failure, 2 usage/ambiguous, 3 not found/not repository, 4 safety refusal (dirty/unpreserved/published/exists/exists_remote/untrusted; refused when the cause is unknown), 5 sync conflict, 6 partial persistent changes. Standalone exec preserves child statuses
When no local branch has that name and exactly one configured remote already has it, create --branch creates the local branch tracking that remote. rabi does not fetch.

When more than one configured remote has the name, create --branch exits 2 and lists those remotes. Pass <remote>/<name>. The remote is a configured remote name. A slash in a branch name is not itself a remote.
<remote>/<name> attaches local branch <name> when that remote is configured and the remote-tracking ref exists. The workspace name omits the remote. An existing local branch keeps its upstream.
A new branch name already present locally or in locally observed remote-tracking refs is refused with exit 4 exists_remote. Use rabi create --branch <name>. rabi does not fetch for this check.

An existing workspace is refused with exit 4 exists unless --reuse matches its source (base/branch/PR and requested issue). Reuse never runs hooks or copies files and preserves existing purpose and creation details; PR reuse can add a missing PR link.

Same-repository PRs use the head branch; fork PRs use owner/head. Fork or deleted heads are fetched from pull/N/head without an upstream. --base, --branch, and --pr are mutually exclusive; --detach cannot accompany --branch or --pr.

--json returns workspace, source (kind new/branch/pr/issue/detach and source details), setup (state, at, ran, ok, command, exitCode, signal, error), copy (copied paths, error), and metadata (ok, error). Failures after checkout creation exit 6.
--no-setup skips copying and hooks; it conflicts with --copy-file.

Copy files from the primary checkout. After exit 6, run the retry command from the error: cd '/absolute/source/checkout' && rabi setup 'SELECTOR'. It preserves the original hook configuration and all --copy-file patterns, using a uniquely resolving name or PR/issue selector. If no selector resolves uniquely, the hint uses (cd WORKSPACE && rabi setup . --source-checkout SOURCE). Run hints in bash or zsh; control characters use ANSI-C quoting ($'...'). --reuse never repeats setup.

notes: With no criterion, --merged, --closed-pr, and --orphaned are all enabled. --older-than only narrows them by createdAt; null creation times are excluded. Without merged PR evidence, a workspace still at its creation commit is not merged.
Without --apply, return plan:true and exit 0 even for protected candidates. data.items entries contain workspace, reasons, action (wouldRemove, removed, skipped, failed), and detail.

After local preservation checks fail, remove and gc can use GitHub evidence for a named branch. A recorded PR (`set --pr` or `create --pr`) must be `MERGED`, and its `headRefOid` must equal the local tip or contain it as an ancestor. Ancestry is checked only when that PR commit already exists locally; nothing is fetched. Partial clones (`extensions.partialClone` configured or any remote with `promisor=true`) require an exact tip match and skip PR object and ancestry probes on every Git version. A recorded URL is passed to `gh` and must match the checkout repository resolved by `gh repo view`; number-only links use that repository. Unlinked branches use one `gh pr list --head BRANCH --state merged --limit 2` query and require exactly one result with the same head name and exact tip ID; ancestry is never used. Repository identity is resolved once per command. Missing or unauthenticated `gh`, failed queries, invalid JSON, ambiguous identities, and timeouts keep the existing local verdict. Each gh call has a 10-second deadline (shorten it with positive `RABI_GH_TIMEOUT_MS`); authentication prompts are disabled and non-interactive stdin is `/dev/null`. Remote responses, including failures, are cached for the command, while local tips and ancestry are rechecked after hooks. JSON items add `preservationReason`: `merged_pr` for GitHub proof, `local` for remove's local proof, otherwise null or absent. Text details identify merged-PR proof. These rules also apply to plans.

Plans and --apply follow remove safety rules: dirty means modified/staged tracked files (including submodule changes) or non-ignored untracked files, matching list/show. Ignored files do not count as dirty and are deleted with the workspace without warning or permission; this also deletes nested Git repositories inside ignored directories (for example, ignored vendor/x/.git). Dirty and unpreserved candidates are skipped; detail gives a targeted rabi remove NAME --discard-changes or rabi remove NAME --delete-unpreserved-branch hint. Permissions are separate and never implied by gc.

Even when clean, workspaces with populated submodules or retained submodule data are refused during remove preflight (exit 4 dirty, including --dry-run) and skipped by gc (plan and --apply) with a rabi remove NAME --discard-changes hint; review the submodule contents, including unpushed commits, before using that permission.
Orphaned records are dropped without deleting checkout files or branches. The current workspace, primary checkout, default branch, and Git-locked checkouts are protected.

Live removal runs trusted [hooks] pre-remove and rechecks the target afterwards. gc never asks for trust; untrusted hooks are skipped unless --no-hooks. A failed candidate does not prevent later candidates from being reported. Failures exit 6 after persistent removal, otherwise 1.
Closed PRs are queried with gh using recorded URLs when available. Missing gh or an unavailable status is reported as unavailable.
Rerunning gc --apply is idempotent; already retired workspaces are no longer candidates.

notes: owner/repo uses github.com. host/owner/repo uses that host.
https URLs, http URLs, ssh:// URLs, and scp-style git@host:owner/repo paths are accepted. A trailing .git suffix is optional.
The repository is placed at <root>/<host>/<owner>/<repo>. The host is lowercased, and a URL port is part of that directory (example.net:9443).

The root is the clone-root key in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rabi/config.toml, otherwise the first git config ghq.root value, otherwise $GHQ_ROOT, otherwise ~/ghq. A configured root is used without reading git config. A git config read failure warns and falls through to $GHQ_ROOT or ~/ghq.
When that path is already the same repository root, rabi registers it and prints the path instead of cloning again. --update fetches origin in that case.
remoteUrl omits http and https userinfo, including a token used as the username. ssh and scp-style URLs keep the login name. file:// URLs and absolute scp-style paths are rejected.
--branch and --depth apply only when cloning. updated is true only when an existing repository was fetched.
If the path exists but is not that repository, the command exits 2 with a usage error.

After clone or fetch, rabi registers the repository. Registration failure exits 6 (partial) if a checkout was created or fetched, retaining repo.root, cloned, and updated in data; otherwise it exits 1. Retrying can register the existing checkout. New workspaces for that repository are created under $XDG_DATA_HOME/rabi/workspaces/<checkout>-<hash> unless workspace-root is set.

Before any fetch or integration, sync checks every configured fetch refspec of every involved remote and refuses with exit 4 refused if a positive refspec has a destination outside refs/remotes/ (including explicit refs/tags/ destinations and mirror mappings). Dangling symbolic refs are omitted by Git's enumeration and are not detected: this is a known limit shared with plain git fetch. Git retains its configured pruning, automatic tag following, negative exclusions and followRemoteHEAD behavior; automatic tag following is not an explicit fetch refspec. Combined dry runs evaluate local bases against tips planned for primary and earlier workspaces, in selection order. Planned branch tips are keyed by full refs: the short branch name refs/heads/a maps to refs/heads/refs/heads/a, independently of branch a at refs/heads/a. examples.description: Retire a workspace
Retire the current workspace
Preview removal
Discard working files explicitly
Delete an unpreserved branch explicitly

notes: SEL is a name, ., pr:N, issue:N, a PR/issue URL, or an absolute path / path starting with ./ or ../. Selectors are required; remove . selects the current workspace. Ambiguous selectors exit 2. The primary checkout always exits 4 primary.

All selectors and safety guards are checked before any hooks or removal. A selector with neither metadata nor a matching Git worktree exits 3 not_found, including with --dry-run; any unknown target aborts all removal and text lists every unknown selector. Modified/staged tracked files (including submodule changes) and non-ignored untracked files exit 4 dirty unless --discard-changes, matching list/show regardless of Git status display settings. Ignored files do not count as dirty and are deleted with the workspace without warning or permission, including with gc --apply. This rule also applies to remove --dry-run and gc plans. Known limitation: nested Git repositories inside ignored directories (for example, vendor/x/.git under ignored vendor/) are also deleted. Unpreserved detached commits exit 4 unpreserved unless --delete-unpreserved-branch.

Even when clean, workspaces with populated submodules or retained submodule data are refused during remove preflight (exit 4 dirty, including --dry-run) and skipped by gc (plan and --apply) with a rabi remove NAME --discard-changes hint; review the submodule contents, including unpushed commits, before using that permission.

After local preservation checks fail, remove and gc can use GitHub evidence for a named branch. A recorded PR (`set --pr` or `create --pr`) must be `MERGED`, and its `headRefOid` must equal the local tip or contain it as an ancestor. Ancestry is checked only when that PR commit already exists locally; nothing is fetched. Partial clones (`extensions.partialClone` configured or any remote with `promisor=true`) require an exact tip match and skip PR object and ancestry probes on every Git version. A recorded URL is passed to `gh` and must match the checkout repository resolved by `gh repo view`; number-only links use that repository. Unlinked branches use one `gh pr list --head BRANCH --state merged --limit 2` query and require exactly one result with the same head name and exact tip ID; ancestry is never used. Repository identity is resolved once per command. Missing or unauthenticated `gh`, failed queries, invalid JSON, ambiguous identities, and timeouts keep the existing local verdict. Each gh call has a 10-second deadline (shorten it with positive `RABI_GH_TIMEOUT_MS`); authentication prompts are disabled and non-interactive stdin is `/dev/null`. Remote responses, including failures, are cached for the command, while local tips and ancestry are rechecked after hooks. JSON items add `preservationReason`: `merged_pr` for GitHub proof, `local` for remove's local proof, otherwise null or absent. Text details identify merged-PR proof. These rules also apply to plans.

Branches are deleted only if integrated into their recorded base (merge, or squash/rebase verified by exact tree entries) or exactly matching their own upstream, or covered by verified merged PR evidence. Squash/rebase evidence uses non-merge commits on the base first-parent history: one complete squash transition, or a distinct base commit for every workspace commit in ancestor-to-tip order, without reusing evidence. Local preservation requires an independent ref in the common Git directory after symbolic-ref resolution; the retiring ref, detached HEAD, and bare commit IDs are insufficient. Otherwise the branch is kept with warning branch_kept_unpreserved and branchKeptReason: unpreserved. --keep-branch always keeps a branch; --delete-unpreserved-branch explicitly allows deleting it.

--dry-run returns plan:true and items with removed:false, wouldRemove and wouldDeleteBranch, without hooks or mutations. JSON data.items contains workspace, removed, branchDeleted, branchKeptReason, detail (the Git error when branch deletion fails), alreadyGone, and error.

If branch deletion fails after checkout removal, remove keeps the branch with warning branch_kept_delete_failed, branchKeptReason: delete_failed, and the Git error in the item detail. This does not fail the item or stop later targets; branch-only failures exit 0 and have no retry command. Decide on any later branch cleanup with Git.

A failure after persistent removal exits 6 and retains every item result. Completed removals also remove their records, so repeating the original command may exit 3. Fix the cause, then run error.details.retryCommand, also shown as Retry with in text. The retry is one invocation: cd <primary> && rabi -R <primary> remove [flags] -- <unfinished paths>. It selects only unfinished checkout or record work, preserves permission flags and output mode, and protects selectors with --. Run hints in bash or zsh; paths are shell-quoted and control characters use ANSI-C quoting. Metadata cleanup is retried only for recorded targets, using the absolute path spelling saved in the record before removal. Location selectors are fixed before removal. A linked checkout supplying pre-remove hooks is removed last; retries preserve its configuration with --source-checkout PATH, which must belong to the selected repository. Once that source is removed, only record cleanup remains and retries disable hooks. Retries add --no-hooks when the original command disabled hooks or its source had no pre-remove hooks, preserving hook non-execution even if primary defines hooks. With -R PRIMARY, dot also resolves a recorded checkout whose Git registration disappeared.

alreadyGone:true requires evidence: a missing directory with metadata and/or an eligible Git registration succeeds, cleaning stale records/registrations without hooks or branch deletion. A record with remaining files but no Git registration also succeeds with alreadyGone:true while retaining files, record and branch. A branch alone or an unregistered directory without a record is insufficient evidence. Removal is limited to linked workspaces inside the resolved directory or recorded paths. Unrecorded external checkouts are refused. Empty parents are cleaned up only below the resolved workspace directory.

.rabi.toml is read from --source-checkout when supplied, otherwise from the invoking checkout (the selected primary checkout with -R/--repo). [hooks] pre-remove commands run in the workspace before it is removed, in order, and stop at the first failure

Hooks and exec receive RABI=1, RABI_WORKSPACE (the workspace name), RABI_WORKSPACE_ID (the ws_ ID, or empty if unrecorded), RABI_WORKSPACE_PATH (the absolute workspace path), and RABI_REPO_PATH (the primary checkout path)

pre-remove hooks run only after the repository is trusted. On a terminal, rabi asks 'Trust this project and run its hooks? [y/N]'. No, a non-terminal, stdin or stderr not being a terminal, nonempty CI, --no-input or RABI_NO_INPUT being enabled, or --json fails before deleting. An empty value counts as unset. Run rabi trust add or pass --no-hooks. RABI_TRUST_ALL=1 trusts every repository for that process and writes nothing

All JSON uses schema 2: {schema:2, command, ok, data, warnings:[{code,message}], error:null|{code,message,details?}}. data preserves partial results and has no top-level version/schema. Parsers must ignore unknown fields. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 operational failure, 2 usage/ambiguous, 3 not found/not repository, 4 safety refusal (dirty/unpreserved/published/exists/exists_remote/untrusted; refused when the cause is unknown), 5 sync conflict, 6 partial persistent changes. Standalone exec preserves child statuses

notes: Uses the checkout containing cwd, or SEL before an explicit --. -R/--repo requires SEL. Primary and orphaned checkouts are refused. The selected repository must be trusted, without prompting, before status inspection.

SEL uses the shared workspace selector rules. At most one positional may precede -- (SEL), and one may follow (TASK). Without --, a single positional remains TASK. Option values, including --skill --, are not separators. Parent cwd and session identity use the selected checkout path.
TASK is optional text; - reads stdin. Later launches resume the recorded parent session; with no message, send Continue. Missing sessions stop with a --fresh hint.

The parent manages progress and its own subagents. Parent exit 0 returns 0 without claiming task completion; Cursor and Claude also require a valid non-error result. Other parent statuses pass through. Timeout exits 124; SIGINT/SIGTERM exits 130. The process group is terminated and reaped. Codex uses TERM then KILL; Cursor and Claude use INT, TERM, KILL and best-effort Linux descendant cleanup; Claude waits 2s after INT and 1s after TERM. Detached Cursor workers may remain; macOS cleanup covers the process group.

Cursor requires cursor-agent (or agent) on PATH and login. It uses --trust --sandbox enabled --auto-review with grok-4.7-high and stdin prompts. Resume requires local chat metadata with hasConversation:true under HOME/.cursor/chats/md5(workspace)/ID/meta.json; missing sessions fail safely with --fresh guidance.

Cursor creates .cursor/sandbox.json with GitHub network domains only when absent, preserves existing user files, and excludes the path through the repository common directory info/exclude. Completed TYPE_INSECURE_NONE tool calls add an audit message and launch.insecureToolCalls count without failing the run. Cursor CLI commit attribution settings are preserved.

Claude Code requires claude on PATH and login (run claude). It uses opus with high effort, stdin prompts, --permission-mode auto --permission-prompts none, and validates init permissionMode as auto. New sessions use a generated UUID recorded as requestedSessionId; resume uses the observed id. No workspace settings are written. Local transcript absence is unknown and still attempts resume. Timeout/interrupt retain 124/130 even for exit-0 error results with null answers.
Text prints the final parent answer. JSON data is {run,launch,answer}; raw stdout and stderr are saved per launch.
